definitions.explanation: The wooden board used for playing the strategy game go ({囲碁|いご}). Standard boards have a 19×19 grid. Also used figuratively to describe grid-like patterns, especially in city planning.

examples.english: To place a stone on the go board.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{愛用|あいよう}→愛用：12693_aiyou⟧⟦していた→する：00392_suru⟧{碁盤|ごばん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}け{継|つ}いだ→受け継ぐ：06700_uketsugu⟧。
examples.english: I inherited the go board my grandfather used to use.

examples.japanese: ⟦{京都|きょうと}→京都：09484_kyouto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{街|まち}→街：17306_machi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{碁盤|ごばん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦のように→のように：30291_noyouni⟧⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{整|ととの}っている→整う：03935_totonou⟧。
examples.english: The streets of Kyoto are laid out in a grid pattern like a go board.

notes:
USAGE:
The expression {碁盤|ごばん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧ (go-board grid) is a common metaphor for a neat grid pattern, especially when describing city street layouts like those of ⟦{京都|きょうと}→京都：09484_kyouto⟧ and ⟦{奈良|なら}→奈良：27451_nara⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {碁盤|ごばん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧: grid pattern (like a go board)
- {碁盤|ごばん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{向|む}かう→向かう：01186_mukau⟧: to sit down at a go board
- {碁盤|ごばん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ような⟦{街|まち}→街：17306_machi⟧: a city with grid-pattern streets
- {碁盤|ごばん}{目状|めじょう}: in a grid pattern
